mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year inflation rate derived from CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as high inflation triggers market concerns about monetary policy tightening and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY inflation rate > 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3.0% and the year-over-year inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the combination of low rates and high inflation creates market uncertainty about the sustainability of the economic expansion and potential for aggressive monetary policy responses.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL YoY inflation rate > 2.0%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL YoY inflation rate > 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 3.5% in the last 3 months), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as the market prices in the expected reduction in liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) are associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as strong housing activity signals a robust economy and increased consumer confidence, which supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high HOUST periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong industrial output indicates a healthy manufacturing sector and rising economic activity, which supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in high INDPRO periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as low unemployment signals a strong labor market and rising consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and equity demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the employment level (PAYEMS) is rising and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is falling, the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the combination signals a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM AND UNRATE < 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
